title: Ground Control Station Technician (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
9.     MOS 5955, Ground Control Station Technician (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Ground Control Station Technicians oversee daily
maintenance production, equipment installation, programing, upgrading, and
troubleshooting on Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Ground Control Station
(GCS) and peripheral Command and Control equipment for the MQ-9 aircraft.
Technicians provide organizational level technical support to facilitate
secure and unsecure, local, and remote flight operations as well as flight
safety, and data collection and dissemination to higher headquarters and
combatant commanders. Technicians are required to ensure all pertinent cyber
security and information security measures are met in accordance with local
and higher headquarters instructions. Technicians are also required to
coordinate with commercial and military Satellite Communication (SATCOM)
Providers to ensure a seamless, on time, secured data link between aircrew
and aircraft. Additional duties include supervision of a maintenance
section/shop, coordination of equipment evacuation for repair with other
maintenance activities, requisitioning of parts, and monitoring maintenance
reports. These technicians also provide technical expertise in the planning,
employment, and installation of aviation communications systems.



                                           3-345                        Enclosure (1)
 3137                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must possess normal color perception.

            (3) Must possess an EL score of 110 or higher.

            (4) Security requirement: secret security clearance eligibility.

       c.   Requirements

            (1) Complete the 5900 Commons Course (M091J31), Twentynine Palms, CA.

        (2) MOS awarded upon certification by the Marines unit CO to DC
Aviation within 6 months or sooner after joining that the Marine has
demonstrated mastery of all 5955 1000-level T&R events contained in NAVMC
3500.128.

    d. Duties. For a complete list of duties and tasks, refer to the Marine
Air Command and Control Systems (MACCS) Maintenance Training and Readiness
(T&R) Manual NAVMC 3500.128.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Radio Operator 27-4013.

            (2) Radio Mechanics 49-2021.

            (3) Computer Operators 43-9011.

            (4) Avionics Technicians 49-2091.

        (5) Electrical and Electronics Repairers, Commercial and Industrial
Equipment 49-2094.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Transmissions Chief, 0629.

            (2) Electronics Maintenance Technician, 2862.

            (3) Aviation Communication Systems Technician, 5939.

            (4) Aviation Meteorological Equipment Technician, 5951.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
